note.en: Ghatotkacha beheads the rakshasa Alayudha in the night battle and casts the head before Duryodhana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CLXXVIII ('Then the mighty son of Bhimasena threw down the head of the slain Alayudha before Duryodhana')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Drona Parva Section CLXXVIII narrates the Ghatotkacha-Alayudha duel and states Bhimasena's son threw the slain Alayudha's head before Duryodhana.

note.en: Alayudha comes to Duryodhana unbidden, offering to fight the Pandavas for him.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CLXXVIII ('Alayudha, having come to Duryodhana of his own accord')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Drona Parva Section CLXXVIII records that Alayudha came to Duryodhana of his own accord to fight for the Kauravas.

note.en: Sunda and Upasunda are brothers born of the Daitya Nikumbha, inseparable until Tilottama divides them.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXI ('Unto this Nikumbha, were born two sons called Sunda and Upasunda')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXI states that two sons, Sunda and Upasunda, were born to the asura Nikumbha.

note.en: Sunda descends through his father Nikumbha from the line of Hiranyakasipu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXI ('Nikumbha, endued with great energy and strength was born in the race of the great Asura, Hiranyakasipu')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXI traces Sunda's father Nikumbha to the race of the asura Hiranyakasipu.

note.en: Sunda and Upasunda quarrel over Tilottama and slay each other, as Brahma had designed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIV ('She is my wife, and therefore your superior, said Sunda')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIV shows Sunda seizing Tilottama and the brothers slaying each other in wrath for her sake.

note.en: Upasunda contends with his brother over Tilottama and both die in the quarrel.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIV ('It was thus that Asuras, ever united and inspired by the same purpose slew each other in wrath for the sake of Tilottama')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIV closes Narada's tale with the two asuras slaying each other for Tilottama's sake.

note.en: Brahma has Viswakarman fashion Tilottama and names her, sending her to divide the asura brothers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIII ('the Grandsire bestowed upon her the name of Tilottama')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIII has Brahma order Viswakarman to create the damsel and bestow on her the name Tilottama.

note.en: Bhima kills the rakshasa Kirmira who bars the Pandavas' path into the forest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Section XI ('Hearing the account of the slaughter in combat of Kirmira, that foremost of Rakshasas')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XI is the Kirmira-badha Parva, in which Vidura recounts Bhima's slaughter of Kirmira.

note.en: Kirmira names himself Baka's brother when he challenges the Pandavas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Section XI ('The Rakshasa thus addressed, answered Yudhishthira the just, saying, I am the brother of Vaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XI has the rakshasa declare to Yudhishthira that he is the brother of Vaka.

note.en: Madhu and Kaitabha are the paired primordial Daityas destroyed together by Vishnu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII narrates Madhu and Kaitabha acting as a pair and being beheaded together by Vishnu's discus.

note.en: Vishnu beheads Kaitabha with his discus after the pair grant him the boon of their own deaths.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII states the Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus.

note.en: Vishnu beheads Madhu with his discus in the same act that ends Kaitabha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII states the Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus.

note.en: Dhundhu, the asura buried in the sea of sands, is reckoned the son of Madhu and Kaitabha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCIII ('The illustrious Dhundhu, O king, was the son of Madhu and Kaitabha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCIII opens by naming Dhundhu the son of Madhu and Kaitabha.

note.en: Dhundhu is named the son of Madhu and Kaitabha, and remembers his father's death at Vishnu's hands.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCIII ('The illustrious Dhundhu, O king, was the son of Madhu and Kaitabha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCIII names Dhundhu the son of Madhu and Kaitabha, remembering his father's death at Vishnu's hands.

note.en: Sthulakesa finds Menaka's abandoned infant, names her Pramadvara and rears her as her foster-father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('the great Brahmana, Sthulakesa, the first of Munis, seeing that female child, and filled with compassion, took it up and reared it')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII has Sthulakesa take up and rear the forsaken child, name her Pramadvara, and betroth her to Ruru as her foster-father.

note.en: Ruru weds Pramadvara after giving her half his own life to recall her from death by snakebite.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('her foster-father betrothed the virgin Pramadvara to Ruru')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII records Sthulakesa betrothing Pramadvara to Ruru, and Ruru begetting a son on her as his wife.

note.en: Sunaka is born to Ruru and Pramadvara.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('And Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII states Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka.

note.en: Pramadvara is Sunaka's mother.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('And Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII states the son Sunaka was begotten on Ruru's wife Pramadvara.

note.en: Ruru stands in the Bhrigu line running through Chyavana, in whose genealogy his son Sunaka is listed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section V ('And to Ruru also by his wife Pramadvara, was born a son, whose name was Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section V gives the Bhrigu genealogy in which Chyavana's line runs down to Ruru and his son Sunaka.

note.en: Sringin is the son of the silent ascetic Samika, whose insult he avenges with a curse.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLII ('Samika repeatedly asked his son to save thee, but there is none to falsify his son's curse')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XLII has Samika speak of Sringin as his son and of his son's irrevocable curse.

note.en: Sringin curses Parikshit to die of Takshaka's bite within seven days for insulting his father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLI ('Seven days hence, Takshaka, the lord of snakes, shall take the sinful king to the horrible abode of Death')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XLI records Sringin's curse that Takshaka would take the king to death in seven days.

note.en: Parikshit hangs a dead snake on the silent Samika's shoulder, the affront that provokes Sringin's curse.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XL ('the king in anger thereupon placed upon his shoulder a dead snake, taking it up with the end of his bow')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XL narrates Parikshit placing a dead snake on the meditating Samika's shoulder.

note.en: Kanwa rears the foundling Shakuntala in his hermitage and she names him her father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXI ('I am the daughter of the virtuous, wise, high-souled, and illustrious ascetic Kanwa')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXI has Shakuntala tell Dushmanta that she is the daughter of the ascetic Kanwa.

note.en: Dushyanta comes to Kanwa's hermitage seeking the sage and finds Shakuntala there instead.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXI ('I have come to worship the highly-blessed Rishi Kanwa')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXI has Dushmanta arrive at the asylum declaring he came to worship the Rishi Kanwa.
